title: How do number lines show where numbers belong?
aliases: where do numbers go on a number line
answer: A number line puts numbers in order and shows how far apart they are. On the usual horizontal line, numbers get larger as you move right. Each step between equally spaced marks has the same size. If you put zero at a mark and count by twos, the next marks to the right are 2, 4 and 6. You can put a number such as 3 halfway between 2 and 4, even if there is no mark there.
facts: A drawing can show just part of a number line, using steps smaller than one.

title: Where does a fraction go on a number line?
aliases: put fractions on a number line
answer: To place three fourths on a number line, divide the space from zero to one into four equal steps. Start at zero and move three of those steps to the right. The bottom number, four, tells you the size of each step. The top number, three, tells you how many steps to take. If the top number is five, keep going past one. Five fourths sits one step past one whole.
facts: Two fourths and one half land on the same point.

title: What is a mixed number?
aliases: what is two and one half
answer: A mixed number joins a whole number and a fraction. Two and one half means two whole things plus half of another. Picture two complete sandwiches and one half sandwich. If you cut the complete sandwiches in half too, you have five halves in all. That is why two and one half and five halves name the same amount. Five halves is called an improper fraction because its top number is greater than its bottom number.
facts: Three and one fourth equals thirteen fourths.

title: How do you add fractions with the same bottom number?
aliases: add one fifth and two fifths
answer: When two fractions describe equal-sized pieces, count how many pieces you have in all. One fifth plus two fifths gives three fifths. Imagine two people coloring one strip of paper that has five equal boxes. If one person colors one box and the other colors two different boxes, three of the five boxes turn colorful. The size of one fifth has stayed the same, so keep five as the bottom number.
facts: Four eighths plus three eighths equals seven eighths.

title: How do you add fractions with different bottom numbers?
aliases: how to add one half plus one quarter
answer: First rewrite the fractions so their pieces are the same size. To add one half and one quarter, imagine two matching paper circles. Cut the half circle into two quarters. Now you have two quarters from the first circle and one from the second, making three quarters altogether. Both fractions are now written with four on the bottom. That shared bottom number is called a common denominator.
facts: One third plus one half equals five sixths.

title: How can a fraction tell you part of a group?
aliases: find a fraction of a number
what is three fourths of twelve
answer: First split the group into equal shares using the bottom number. Then count as many shares as the top number asks for. For three fourths of 12 pencils, make four equal piles of three. Choose three of those piles. They hold nine pencils together. The whole group is 12 pencils, and every one of the four equal shares has exactly three. A fraction can describe part of a group as well as part of a single object.
facts: Two thirds of 15 paper clips is 10 paper clips.

title: How do you turn a fraction into a decimal?
aliases: convert a fraction to a decimal
how do i write three quarters as a decimal
answer: A fraction bar can stand for division. To write three fourths as a decimal, divide three by four. Imagine sharing three dollars between four people. Everyone gets 75 cents, so the amount for each is 0.75 dollars. That is the same number as three fourths. Some decimal answers stop, like 0.75, while other answers keep repeating a pattern of digits, like the threes in one third.
facts: One half is 0.5, which can also be written as 0.50.

title: Why do some decimal digits repeat forever?
aliases: why is one third point three three three
answer: When you divide one by three, the first digit after the decimal point is three. The division leaves a remainder of one in the current place. Bringing down another zero gives you the same situation again, so you get another three. The same remainder keeps turning up and the threes keep going. Other fractions repeat a longer pattern. For example, two elevenths repeats the pair 18.
facts: The repeating part of one sixth is just the six, after an initial one.

title: What does a ratio compare?
answer: A ratio describes how one amount compares with another. If a box has two green markers and three purple markers, the ratio of green to purple is two to three. Another box with four green and six purple markers has the same ratio. Both amounts doubled, so the color mix stayed the same. Order matters. Purple to green is three to two. Green to all the markers is two to five, because the whole box contains five.
facts: The same ratio can describe groups of different sizes.

title: What does “per one” mean in a unit rate?
answer: A unit rate tells you how much of one thing goes with one unit of another. If a game hands out 24 cards in four equal rounds, divide 24 by four. That gives six cards per round. If three identical notebooks cost nine dollars altogether, the price is three dollars per notebook. “Per” means “for each” here. A unit rate makes it easier to compare groups that come in different sizes.
facts: Speed can be given in units such as miles per hour or meters per second.

title: What are the parts of a division problem called?
aliases: what are dividend divisor and quotient
answer: In 24 ÷ 6 = 4, the number 24 is the amount you start with. It is called the dividend. The number six is the divisor. It can tell you how many equal groups to make, or how big each group should be. Four is the quotient, which here tells you the answer to the division. Think of sharing 24 stickers among six friends. Each friend gets four stickers.

title: How can you tell if a number divides evenly?
aliases: how to tell if a number divides by three
answer: Some divisors have short tests. A number divides evenly by two if its last digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. To check for five, look for a last digit of zero or five. To check for three, add the digits and see whether their sum divides evenly by three. The digits of 516 add up to 12, so 516 divides evenly by three. These tests let you decide without doing the full division.
facts: A whole number divides evenly by ten if its last digit is zero.

title: How does a factor tree break a number into primes?
aliases: how to make a factor tree
write a number as a product of primes
answer: A factor tree starts with a number and splits it into two smaller factors greater than one. Start with 36 and split it into six times six. Each six splits into two times three. Two and three are prime, which means they cannot be split again this way. The leaves of the tree give two times three times two times three. That product is the prime factorization of 36.
facts: Starting 36 with four times nine gives the same prime factors in a different order.

title: What is the greatest common factor?
answer: The greatest common factor is the largest whole number that divides evenly into each of the numbers you are checking. Say you want to use 12 red beads and 18 blue beads to make identical bracelets, with none left over. Six is the greatest common factor of 12 and 18. You can make six bracelets, each with two red and three blue beads. No larger number of identical bracelets uses all of both colors.
facts: The greatest common factor of eight and 12 is four.

title: What is the least common multiple?
aliases: when do two repeating events happen together
answer: The least common multiple is the smallest positive number that appears in two lists of multiples. Think of two lights that flash together now. One flashes every four seconds and the other every six seconds. The first light flashes at 4, 8 and 12 seconds. The second flashes at 6 and 12 seconds. They next flash together after 12 seconds. Twelve is the least common multiple of four and six.
facts: The least common multiple of two and five is ten.

title: What does absolute value measure?
aliases: what does absolute value of negative four mean
answer: Absolute value measures a number’s distance from zero. On a number line, negative four is four steps to the left of zero and positive four is four steps to the right. Both are the same distance away, so both have absolute value four. Imagine a line of tape on the floor with a dot at zero. Walk four steps in either direction from that dot. The distance from your starting mark does not depend on which way you went.
facts: The absolute value of zero is zero.

title: How do the greater-than and less-than signs work?

which way does the inequality sign go
what does the less than sign mean
answer: The wide opening faces the greater number and the point faces the smaller one. In 4 < 9, the opening faces nine, so read it as four is less than nine. You can also write 9 > 4 and read it as nine is greater than four. On a number line, the greater number is farther right. That works even below zero. Negative two is greater than negative five because negative two sits to its right.

title: What does the equal sign really mean?
aliases: why is seven equals three plus four true
what does the equals sign tell us
answer: The equal sign says that the quantities on both sides have the same value. In 3 + 4 = 7, each side has the value seven. It is just as true to write 7 = 3 + 4. Both sides can even have more than one number. In 4 + 5 = 6 + 3, each side has the value nine. Think of two trays holding different piles but the same total number of blocks. The piles look different, and the amounts are equal.

title: What is the difference between an expression and an equation?
aliases: what is an expression in math
answer: An expression names a value. For example, 4 + 3 is an expression that names seven. An equation says two expressions have equal values, as in 4 + 3 = 7. Think of a label that tells you how many blocks are in a jar. That label can be an expression. To say the jar holds as many blocks as another jar, you can use an equation. Expressions and equations can also use a letter to stand for a number.

title: When can you swap numbers without changing the answer?
aliases: why can you swap the order when adding
answer: You can swap the order of two numbers when adding or multiplying them and still get the same answer. Three groups of five tiles and five groups of three tiles both make 15 tiles. You can see this by turning a rectangle of tiles a quarter turn. The rows and columns trade jobs. This is called the commutative property. Subtraction works differently. Seven minus three gives four, but three minus seven gives negative four.
facts: Six plus two and two plus six both equal eight.

title: When can you group numbers in a different way?
aliases: which numbers can i add first
answer: When you add three numbers, you can choose which pair to add first while keeping the numbers in the same order. For five plus eight plus two, you might add eight and two first because they make ten. The total is still 15. This is called the associative property. It also works for multiplication. Grouping can make a calculation easier in your head. The same trick does not always work when subtracting.
facts: Grouping 2 × 5 first makes 2 × 5 × 7 easy to calculate as 10 × 7.

title: What does the small raised number in a power mean?
aliases: what does two to the fourth power mean
answer: A small raised number can tell you how many copies of the same number to multiply. In 2⁴, the big two is called the base and the little four is the exponent. Multiply four copies of two together: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. The answer is 16. Two to the fourth power means repeated multiplication. Two times four is a different calculation and gives eight. Read the small number as part of the power, not as another number in a single multiplication.

title: What happens when a shape slides across a grid?

answer: A slide, or translation, moves every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction. If the left corner of a triangle moves three spaces right and one space up, each of the other corners moves three spaces right and one space up too. title: When are two shapes exactly the same size and shape?

answer: Two shapes are congruent if you can make one fit exactly over the other by moving it, turning it or flipping it. Cut two triangles from the same cardboard pattern.
